items.title: Albert Jiles Interview, 1960-06-15
items.q: He took me and Peter Pappy and Georgie Boyd.

ctx.x: After you studied, say a couple of years, when did you start playing any jobs with the real band, not necessarily professional, or that is to get paid for, but when did you join any small group or brass band? Can you remember what you'd say is your first job or your first orchestra?

Well, after I got the drum, as I told you, my uncle got the drum from a forum shop. I was going to Lansing. I had a fellow come to bring society notice to my house. His name was Lawrence Randall. He said, I told him I had a drum. He said, well, I got a trumpet. I'm learning how to play music. He said, I'm thinking about going to Old Man Chalini. And I told him it was a good idea to go over there. And so he said, of course, I've been getting a little lessons from my uncle, Joe Nicholas. I said, yeah? I said, yeah.…
I don't want to interrupt you, but I'll never think of it again. How was Faiso as a drummer?

items.title: Albert Jiles Interview, 1961-02-24
items.q: Well Eddie, trombone player, Peter Pappy, playing clarinet. Peter Pappy playing banjo, Zeb. Johnny Prydoch playing bass at the time when I played with him.

ctx.x: uh 24. So it was after World War I anyway. Oh yeah. You were about 19 or 20 or maybe 18. Um 17. About 17. So let's see. Did you ever work with a

kid Rene? Did you ever know him? Oh yeah. I worked often and on when Joe was sick or he had two jobs. I worked with Rene, Kid Rene. They have a pretty good band? Yeah, yeah. Great band. And they had one of the top bands. Who was in it? Well Eddie, trombone player, Peter Pappy, playing clarinet. Peter Pappy playing banjo, Zeb. Johnny Prydoch playing bass at the time when I played with him. That'd be a band. Unless they had saxophone. He did. Manny Gabriel, he was playing saxophone. Violin? Have any violins? No, he…

did he live? Oh Eddie Marsh. Eddie Marsh, he's still alive. Yeah. I think Eddie lives, I don't know, somewhere about. Oh yeah, St. Phillip. Yeah, up there. I just wondered if it was the same guy.
